# core:process

Run a host program, confined to the guest's own grants.

A child reads and writes only beneath the directories the guest was
granted, plus a fixed system baseline (the loader, shared libraries,
installed programs), and reaches the network only where the guest does.
Spawning never extends the guest's authority. The host offers it only where
its OS can enforce that, and [`availability`] says whether this one does.
Every other function requires it to answer `Available`, and traps
otherwise. See WEP 2026-10-21 (`core:process`).

A child's output is bytes, so it comes back as a `ByteList`, never decoded.

## Synopsis

```wado
if availability() != Availability::Available {
    return;
}
let out = cmd`echo hello`.read().unwrap();
assert out == b"hello\n";
```

## Globals

### `pub global DEFAULT_CAPTURE_LIMIT: i32`

How many bytes `output` and `read` keep of each stream unless a
[`Command::capture_limit`] says otherwise.

## Functions

### `pub fn availability() -> Availability with Process`

Whether this host spawns. The answer is fixed for the guest's lifetime.

### `pub fn cmd<T: ReflectTemplate<Holes = [..V]>, ..V: CmdArg>(t: T) -> Command`

A `Command` from an argument vector, built without a shell.

Literal text splits on whitespace. A hole is exactly one argument, whatever
it holds, and a `List<String>` hole one per element. Parts with no
whitespace between them join into one argument; a `List<String>` hole
joined to anything is a contract violation. So is literal text holding a
character a shell would treat specially (quotes, `\`, `|`, `&`, `;`, `<`,
`>`, parentheses, braces, `$`, a backtick, `~`, `*`, `?`, brackets, `#`):
here it would mean nothing. A value holding one goes through a hole.

## Effects

### `pub interface Process`

Spawning a child confined to the guest's grants plus a fixed system
baseline: spawning never extends the guest's authority.

Every function but `get-availability` requires it to answer `available`,
and traps otherwise.

#### `fn get_availability() -> Availability`

`#[cm("core:process/process@0.1.0#get-availability")]`

Whether spawning is offered, with no side effect.

`#[cm("core:process/process@0.1.0#spawn")]` `#[cm_params("cmd", "cwd")]`

Start `cmd` in `cwd`, or in the first preopened directory with `none`.

## Structs

### `pub struct Command`

A program to run and how: its arguments, environment, streams and timeout.

A child gets no stream of the guest's unless asked: stdin reads nothing,
and its stdout and stderr go nowhere. `output` and `read` pipe what they
read themselves.

_Fields are private._

#### `pub fn new(program: String) -> Command`

`program` holding a `/` is a path, relative to where the child starts.
Any other is looked up on the host's `PATH`.

#### `pub fn arg(&self, arg: String) -> Command`

#### `pub fn args(&self, args: List<String>) -> Command`

#### `pub fn env(&self, key: String, value: String) -> Command`

Set `key` in the child's environment, over the baseline the host
gives it (`PATH`, a private `HOME` and `TMPDIR`, the locale). The
guest's own environment is never passed on.

#### `pub fn stdin_piped(&self) -> Command`

`spawn` hands the guest the child's stdin as `Child::stdin`.

#### `pub fn stdout_piped(&self) -> Command`

`spawn` hands the guest the child's stdout as `Child::stdout`.

#### `pub fn stderr_piped(&self) -> Command`

`spawn` hands the guest the child's stderr as `Child::stderr`.

#### `pub fn inherit_stdin(&self) -> Command with Stdin`

The child reads the guest's own stdin, which the guest passes on only
where it holds it.

#### `pub fn inherit_stdout(&self) -> Command with Stdout`

The child writes to the guest's own stdout.

#### `pub fn inherit_stderr(&self) -> Command with Stderr`

The child writes to the guest's own stderr.

#### `pub fn inherit_stdio(&self) -> Command with (Stdin, Stdout, Stderr)`

All three of the guest's own streams.

#### `pub fn timeout(&self, timeout: Duration) -> Command`

End the child at `timeout`: the host sends its process group
`SIGTERM`, then `SIGKILL` after a grace period, and it exits
`ExitStatus::TimedOut`. There is no default.

#### `pub fn capture_limit(&self, bytes: i32) -> Command`

- `contract bytes >= 0`

The bytes `output` and `read` keep of each stream. Past it, stderr
keeps its tail, and stdout is an `OutputTooLarge` error: the host
kills the child the moment stdout passes it.

#### `pub fn spawn(&self) -> Result<Child, ProcessError> with Process`

Start the child and hand back its piped streams.

#### `pub fn output(&self) -> Result<Output, ProcessError> with Process`

Run the child to its end, reading stdout and stderr together. A
timeout is not an error: the status says `TimedOut`, beside what was
read.

#### `pub fn status(&self) -> Result<ExitStatus, ProcessError> with Process`

Run the child to its end and return how it ended.

#### `pub fn read(&self) -> Result<ByteList, ProcessError> with Process`

Run the child to its end and return its stdout. Any end but
`Exited(0)` is `Failed`, with the stderr read beside it.

### `pub affine struct Child`

A running child. Dropping it kills its process group, and the host kills
every child when the guest exits, so a child never outlives its guest.

#### `stdin: Option<StreamWritable<u8>>`

Where `Command::stdin_piped` asked for it. Dropping it closes the
child's stdin.

#### `stdout: Option<Stream<u8>>`

Where `Command::stdout_piped` asked for it.

#### `stderr: Option<Stream<u8>>`

Where `Command::stderr_piped` asked for it.

#### `pub fn wait(self) -> Result<ExitStatus, ProcessError>`

Wait for the child to end. Nothing can reach a stream still left in the
`Child` once it is waited on, so `wait` closes each first: take a piped
stream out to use it.

#### `pub fn kill(&self)`

Kill the child's process group now.

## Variants

### `pub variant ProcessErrorKind`

#### `NotFound`

No such program, on `PATH` or at the path given.

#### `NotPermitted`

The sandbox refused to execute the program: it lies outside the
grants and the baseline.

#### `Io(ErrorCode)`

#### `Failed([ExitStatus, ByteList])`

`read` only: the child ended other than `Exited(0)`, with what it
wrote to stderr.

#### `OutputTooLarge`

Stdout passed the capture limit, and the child was killed.

### `pub variant CmdArgs`

One hole of a [`cmd`] template: one argument, or one per element.

#### `One(String)`

#### `Each(List<String>)`

### `pub variant ExitStatus`

How a child ended.

#### `Exited(u8)`

It exited with this status.

#### `Signaled(u8)`

A signal ended it.

#### `TimedOut`

The host ended it at its timeout.
